paragraphs: Here's what I love about David in this chapter, friend. Every time something big comes up, he asks the LORD first (1 Samuel 23:2, 4, 9-12). Even when his men are scared, he doesn't just trust his gut, he asks again. And the LORD answers him every time, whether it's "Go at once to Keilah" or a hard answer he didn't want to hear (1 Samuel 23:4, 11-12).

Now, that hard answer is the part that stings. David saved Keilah, and the LORD told him the town would still hand him over (1 Samuel 23:12). So David left, and he didn't get stuck in the hurt. Being told the truth early let him move before the trap closed, and that's how I read it. God's guidance isn't always the nice news, but it's the news you can build on.

Then look at how it ends, with Saul closing in on one side of the mountain and David hurrying on the other (1 Samuel 23:26). A messenger shows up with news of a raid, and Saul turns away (1 Samuel 23:27-28). Day after day Saul searched, "but God would not deliver David into his hand" (1 Samuel 23:14). Before that, Jonathan walked into the wilderness to strengthen David's hand in God (1 Samuel 23:16). So when you're running, baker, ask the LORD first, take the friend He sends, and trust that He's holding you even when the hill feels way too small. And this story isn't over.
